tasks.short: Prepare health course syllabi, assignments and handouts

steps.what: Choose learning outcomes, scope and teaching sequence
Read and verify current clinical sources and examples
Copy current course dates and policy blocks into the syllabus
Write homework questions, explanations and clinical teaching examples

loop.input: Chosen outcomes, verified source passages and teacher's example constraints
loop.output: Draft questions, handouts and explanations linked to their source passages
loop.check: Teacher checks clinical meaning, answerability, difficulty, current guidance and source support in s6; s4 includes rewriting unsuitable examples
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, then manual composition
loop.why_not_simpler: Use current reusable material first; new explanatory prose and examples cannot be assembled from fixed fields alone

steps.what: Format the syllabus, assignments and handouts for use
Check clinical accuracy, pedagogical meaning and accessibility of final materials
Save the prepared materials in the same document store

tasks.design: Test native {DOCS} templates for current syllabus fields and reusable formatting, using verified course data from {LMS}. Offer a bounded draft of new prose from teacher-selected clinical sources, followed by full clinical and pedagogical checking; ordinary saving remains unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated syllabus fields and formatting were interleaved with clinically sensitive writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates handle exact fields, while bounded drafting can express selected source material.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible teaching example may misstate a clinical condition or imply an unsafe action.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher chooses what students must understand and judges clinical nuance.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat assembly and first-draft prose; curriculum and clinical judgement stay with the teacher.

reach.task: Align a clinical assignment with learning outcomes

evidence.claim: Bounded source-based drafting and native syllabus templates are feasible design components; the health-course implementation and time estimates are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation of actual course materials, not delivery or publication. No patient information is needed; examples use teacher-created fictional cases or permitted published material.

Course administration supplies course ID, dates, contact details and approved policy version; the teacher verifies applicability in s1 and reads clinical sources in s2. Missing metadata is entered manually in retained planning time, not extracted for free.

Ten assembly hours are repeat dates and fixed policy blocks. Of twenty-five writing hours, ten are initial prose composition and fifteen remain for original questions, revision and custom cases. Of ten formatting hours, five are repeated styles and five remain for diagrams, layout repairs and accessibility checks.
All nineteen final clinical-check hours remain. The one-hour author save is retained and ungated. Native templates precede custom code; existing rendering runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: How much material is already reused
Clinical source access and review policy
Actual repeat field and formatting work
research_questions: Which material sections can be assembled without generating new clinical claims?
Does drafting reduce composition after all clinical corrections?

already_counted.description: Rewrite drafts and verify final clinical and pedagogical meaning

incremental.description: Maintain source restrictions, templates and course metadata mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is ten assembly, ten prose and five formatting hours, less three upkeep = 22. Cautious case: a new clinical course needs all prose written manually and its policy blocks are bespoke, retaining s3 and s4 in full; only five formatting hours are removed, less three upkeep = 2.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Stay current through literature, colleagues and conferences

steps.what: Search for relevant current health literature and select papers
Read current literature and critically assess methods and findings
Discuss developments and their limits with colleagues
Participate in professional conferences and question emerging findings

tasks.design: Configure saved specialty searches and new-publication filters in the literature catalogue {OTHER}. The teacher still selects and reads original papers, talks with colleagues and participates in conferences; no new digest or learning log is required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue queries can consume time before any critical reading begins.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved searches and duplicate filtering can surface bibliographic candidates without summarising findings.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence quality, clinical relevance and disagreement require original reading and discussion.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher distinguishes a promising claim from evidence worth teaching.
tasks.altitude: Some repeated searching falls away; reading and professional relationships keep their place in the week.

reach.learn: Controlled vocabulary, source coverage and search recall

evidence.claim: Saved catalogue searches can reduce repeated query entry while retaining critical reading; this is model knowledge, with no claimed study time effect.

assumptions: Boundary is finding and learning from developments, not research synthesis or course revision. No record write, report or send is assumed in ordinary reading and discussion; actual conference booking is outside attendance and receives no saving here.

The teacher supplies specialty terms, relevant journals, date window and exclusion criteria in the existing search workflow. The literature catalogue supplies title, identifier, date and abstract; unavailable or incomplete metadata requires manual searching within retained s1 time.

Of fifteen search hours, 4.5 are repeating established queries and excluding exact duplicates; 10.5 remain for screening relevance and new searches. Native configuration is tried first; no model summary substitutes for any of fifty reading hours.
unknowns: Whether topic changes make saved queries obsolete
research_questions: Does a saved specialty query recover important new papers without excessive screening?

already_counted.description: Screen candidates and search new topics manually

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is 4.5 repeated-search hours less 0.5 upkeep = 4. If the specialty question changes each time or current alerts already cover it, retain all fifteen search hours and do not add the configuration, giving zero. Literature reading, discussion and conferences are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate assignments and papers and release checked grades

steps.what: Read students' class work, assignments and papers against the rubric
Evaluate clinical reasoning and choose rubric scores and grades
Enter the chosen grades and specific instructor feedback notes
Compose feedback explaining the instructor's findings

loop.input: Instructor-entered findings, rubric and quoted submission passages
loop.output: Feedback expressing only the instructor's findings without changing the grade
loop.check: Teacher edits in s4 and checks every claim, clinical explanation, tone and score consistency in s5
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or changed grading trigger manual feedback
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed comments are tried first; explaining case-specific reasoning in clear language needs bounded prose drafting

steps.what: Check final grades, feedback, recipients and release version
Re-key approved grades into the separate student registry {OTHER}
Send the approved grade and feedback release to the named students

tasks.design: The teacher reads, grades and first records findings in {LMS}; a bounded loop drafts feedback from those recorded findings. After checking the exact final result snapshot, a native connector transfers it to the separate student registry {OTHER} and a separate gated release sends the results to the approved students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing explanations and re-keying checked grades were mixed with substantive grading.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructor-note-based feedback drafting and deterministic result transfer can be separated from grade decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical reasoning, borderline performance and misleading explanations require the examiner's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher understands the student's reasoning and takes responsibility for the grade and explanation.
tasks.altitude: Less feedback composition and duplicate entry, while every grade decision remains human.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; this supports note-based drafting rather than autonomous grading.
The digest describes Radboud requiring grades in both Brightspace and OSIRIS; this supports the existence of a two-system workflow, not its prevalence or these timings.
The proposed labour shares and retained checks are model knowledge and must be verified locally.

assumptions: Boundary includes substantive marking, first grade and note entry, actual feedback composition, a real second-system grade re-key and student result release. Use this branch only where the teacher actually performs that second entry; no such baseline is presumed from the job title alone.

Students supply submissions. The teacher supplies every score, quoted issue and feedback finding in s3, whose full first-capture time remains. Student administration maintains student ID, course ID, assessment ID and registry target mapping; the teacher verifies exact recipients and values in s5. Missing mappings require manual transfer, not a free repaired feed.

Ten of twenty feedback hours remain for editing; all ten final check hours remain. Nine transfer hours are repeated grade entry into a genuinely separate registry, not a same-system author save. Ordinary saving stays inside unchanged s3/s4 time, with no self-gate or saving.

Test existing comment banks and native connector configuration first. The s5 snapshot binds scores, feedback text, student IDs, assessment IDs and destinations; edits invalidate both action approvals. Failed transfer or rejected release returns to the teacher rather than guessing.
unknowns: Whether the teacher actually re-keys into a second registry
Actual feedback composition and final check time
research_questions: Do note-based drafts preserve clinical meaning after all corrections?
Can the native result connector validate exact IDs without a new manual reconciliation workload?

already_counted.description: Edit explanations and check final grade, meaning and recipients

incremental.description: Handle connector failures and maintain assessment mappings and draft restrictions

approvals.approved_version: s5 final immutable result snapshot including grades, student and assessment IDs and registry destination; any edit voids approval
s5 final immutable result snapshot including exact grade, feedback text, named student recipients and release channel; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is ten feedback-composition hours, nine second-registry entry hours and one real student send hour, less two upkeep = 18. Cautious case: complex clinical papers require all twenty feedback hours manually, while verified second-registry entry and real release still remove ten, less two upkeep = 8. If there is no second entry, remove that opportunity and remeasure before using this estimate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the current laboratory protocol and identify session hazards
Check laboratory conditions and demonstrate safe technique
Supervise laboratory practice and intervene when students need help
Debrief techniques, errors and questions with students

tasks.design: Keep direct laboratory supervision and debriefing with the teacher, using the current protocol in {DOCS}. Source reading is already direct; the task contains no routine record or send that this design changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is real-time observation, demonstration and intervention rather than repeated information processing.
tasks.enabler_now: No new component removes an actual step without losing supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Safe technique and timely intervention depend on what students do in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices unsafe practice and adapts a demonstration immediately.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in supervision time or decision rights.

evidence.claim: Physical laboratory supervision and immediate intervention remain human work; this is model knowledge, not a measured baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is supervision of an existing laboratory session, including actual protocol reading and live debrief. Course material preparation is separately present in 6103, and any formal grading is separately present in 6102; neither is silently removed from this task.
The current approved protocol is supplied by the course owner and read in s1; absent or unclear instructions require direct clarification in retained time. No new data feed is assumed.

Checked for actual record writes, reports and sends before assigning zero: routine attendance, assessment, booking or incident reporting is not assumed in this supervision baseline. If a specific session requires an incident record or assessment, price its real first capture and any send separately; do not create a trailing log for every session.
All current source reading, physical checks, demonstration, supervision and conversation remain. No tool is deployed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which sessions require a real incident or assessment record
research_questions: Is any separate record or send actually performed by the teacher during these sessions?

incremental.description: No new tool or maintained configuration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All one hundred hours remain. Direct protocol access already exists and no changed record, report, send or physical activity has been identified, so there is no eligible saving or upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps clinical source interpretation, grading decisions and laboratory supervision. Repeat course assembly, feedback prose and genuine second-system grade entry may shrink after local checks.
reach: Work with an instructional coordinator on clinical assessment validity
skills_to_grow: Check feedback meaning and result destinations
role.ambitious_version: A clinical educator with more reliable course assembly and feedback handling while retaining direct responsibility for learning and safety.
